title: International Olympic Committee consensus statement on thermoregulatory and altitude challenges for high-level athletes
publisher: International Olympic Committee Medical Commission / British Journal of Sports Medicine
claims: Arriving two weeks before competition at moderate altitude, with one or two days of rest before regular training, is the typical recommended approach.
At moderate altitude most athletes acclimatise within two weeks; partial acclimatisation with improved performance can be achieved within 5 to 7 days.
Most athletic events are held at altitudes that pose little or no health risk, but even modest altitude can affect performance.
Altitude ranges are conventionally described as low (500-2000 m), moderate (2000-3000 m) and high (3000-5500 m).
